title: Pre-Purchase Ship Inspection Shanghai | Yangtze Estuary & Yards
description: Pre-purchase inspection in Shanghai: buyers' condition and thickness readings on bulk carriers in the Yangtze estuary, container ships and docked ships.
h1: Pre-Purchase Inspection of Ships Bought in Shanghai: Estuary Anchorages, Terminals and Yards
intro: Shanghai is a centre of Chinese shipowning and ship leasing, and a great many second-hand purchases are decided by people in the city. The ship itself may be waiting at the Yangtze estuary anchorages, working cargo at Yangshan or Waigaoqiao, or docked at a lower Yangtze yard. Each setting gives a buyer a different view of her, and the short calls of the container trade give the least. Atlantis carries out pre-purchase inspections in all three settings, sending its team from India on Chinese business visas, which is why an early viewing date matters here more than in most ports.

highlights.p: Bulk carriers and ore carriers often wait at the estuary anchorages for a berth or for river passage. In ballast and idle, they are the easiest ships to inspect properly: holds, ballast tanks and machinery can all be reached with the crew's help.

highlights.h: Visa lead time sets the plan
highlights.p: Technicians travel on Chinese business visas issued against an invitation letter, so the date the ship can be boarded is only half the plan. Sending the vessel name as soon as the inspection is agreed in principle gives the paperwork time to catch up.

highlights.h: Lessors and Chinese owners as buyers
highlights.p: Shanghai's leasing companies and shipowners buy second-hand tonnage and finance it for others. Both want a condition record that their technical teams and credit committees can follow without having boarded, with every reading located and every photograph tied to a space.

sections.h: Where can a second-hand ship be inspected in the Shanghai port system?
p: The Yangtze estuary anchorages are where buyers see the most. Bulk carriers, ore carriers and tankers wait there for berths or for passage upriver, often in ballast, and the seller's agent arranges a launch to the ship's position. Holds can be cleaned and ventilated, ballast tanks certified for entry and the engine room shown with the generators and pumps running.

The container terminals at Yangshan and Waigaoqiao give the least. Calls are tightly scheduled, cargo stays on board and the crane plan governs the deck, so a buyer's visit to a container ship there covers what the crew can show without interrupting cargo work: weather deck, hatch coamings, lashing structure, engine room and the scrubber system if one is fitted. Tankers at the oil and petrochemical terminals around the estuary can be inspected on deck and in the machinery spaces, with tank entry only where gas-free certificates allow.

Repair yards on the lower Yangtze and in the Zhoushan archipelago give the most complete view when a seller docks the ship before delivery. Shanghai's own large yards concentrate on newbuilding, so the docking, if there is one, is usually some distance from the city.
list: Yangtze estuary anchorages: holds, ballast tanks, deck and machinery on bulk carriers, ore carriers and tankers
Yangshan Deep-Water Port: deck, coamings, lashing structure and engine room on mainline container ships
Waigaoqiao terminals: feeders and intra-Asia container ships, sometimes with ballast tanks released
Estuary oil and petrochemical terminals: deck and machinery on product and chemical tankers
Lower Yangtze and Zhoushan repair yards: dry hull and open tanks when the seller docks before delivery

sections.h: Who buys second-hand ships through Shanghai, and what do they need to know?
p: Chinese owners are active buyers of second-hand bulk carriers and tankers, and Shanghai's leasing companies buy ships in sale-and-leaseback deals or hold them as security. Foreign buyers inspect ships here as well, because a Chinese-owned ship on a Yangtze or coastal trade may be most easily seen at the estuary. The buyer's questions do not change with nationality: what will the next renewal survey ask for, how sound are the ballast tanks, and does the machinery run as the records claim?

Many of the bulk carriers and ore carriers viewed here were built in Chinese yards and have carried coal and iron ore into China for most of their lives. That trade is hard on holds: tank tops and hopper plating take damage from grabs and bulldozers, and lower frames suffer under the cargo. A buyer looking at such a ship needs measured evidence of how far the steel has gone, not just photographs of clean holds.

Container ships change hands through Shanghai too, often between non-operating owners and lessors while the ship stays on charter. On those deals the inspection usually has to fit a single berth call, so the buyer's priorities are agreed before the ship arrives.

sections.h: Arranging access in Shanghai: visas, the agent and the estuary weather
p: The invitation letter and Chinese business visa are the longest step for a team travelling from India, and they cannot be rushed at the end. The seller's agent arranges terminal passes for Yangshan or Waigaoqiao and the launch for an anchorage visit, and confirms what the port authorities need before anyone boards a ship at anchor.

Weather in the estuary deserves a margin. Dense fog, most frequent in the cooler months, can suspend shipping and launch services for hours or longer, and summer brings the risk of typhoons. Tidal streams in the river mouth also affect when a launch can come alongside safely. Where the sale terms fix a short inspection period, the brokers should know that the estuary may not cooperate on the planned day.

Port state control in Shanghai is carried out by the China Maritime Safety Administration under the Tokyo MoU, and the ship's inspection history is published. Reading it before the visit shows whether structural, fire-main or ballast-piping items have been raised before, which in turn shows where the readings should go.

sections.h: What does a buyer's inspection usually find on ships at Shanghai?
p: On bulk carriers and ore carriers from the China trades, hold tank tops and hopper plating show grab and machinery damage, lower frames and brackets are wasted or distorted, and hatch covers on heavily cycled ships show worn packing and corroded drain channels. Topside ballast tanks commonly show coating breakdown on their upper parts and along stiffener edges.

On container ships, the usual items are coaming top wastage, cracking at hatch corners and lashing bridge supports, and erosion in scrubber wash-water lines where the system has worked hard in open-loop mode at sea. Product tankers bring ballast tank coatings and deck piping into focus, and older ones fire main and sea-water lines with a record of pinhole repairs. Each finding is photographed against its location and read against the last thickness report the seller releases through class.

China Classification Society classes many of the ships seen here. Its records reach the buyer the same way as those of any other society, through the society and with the seller's consent, and the buyer reviews them with our notes on how the readings taken on board compare.

sections.h: Worked scope: a Capesize bulk carrier at the estuary anchorage
p: Take a Capesize bulk carrier in her mid-teens waiting at the estuary anchorage in ballast, with a Chinese buyer's superintendent and a lessor's representative due to attend. The seller agrees to prepare a number of holds and the topside and hopper tanks between them, and the chief engineer will run the generators and the main ballast pumps.

In the holds, the team photographs and gauges the tank top, hopper plating and lower bulkhead strakes, examines frame ends and brackets, and checks the hatch corners for cracks where a patch may be cleaned. In the ballast tanks it rates the coatings and takes readings at the bottom and the upper parts. Hatch covers are checked for packing, cleats and drainage. The report sets the readings beside the last renewal survey results and lists the holds the seller did not open.

None of these readings counts towards a class survey. They inform the buyer and the negotiation; class credit needs a thickness firm holding IACS UR Z17 approval from the ship's own society, an approval Atlantis is in the process of obtaining from DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS.

Mainline container ships sold while on charter

IACS UR S21 – hatch covers, hatch coamings and closing arrangements of bulk carriers

faqs.q: Can you inspect a bulk carrier waiting at the Yangtze estuary anchorage for a buyer?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is often the best setting in Shanghai. A ship waiting in ballast for a berth or river passage can prepare holds and ballast tanks and run her generators for machinery readings. The seller's agent arranges the launch. Tell us the expected anchorage period so the plan can allow for fog or launch delays in the estuary.

faqs.q: How much notice do you need for a pre-purchase inspection in Shanghai?
faqs.a: The visa sets the notice. Technicians travel on Chinese business visas issued against an invitation letter, which takes longer than the journey itself. Send the IMO number and the likely viewing window to info@atlantisndt.com as soon as the inspection is agreed in principle, even if the dates may move, and we start the paperwork straight away.

faqs.q: Can a container ship be inspected at Yangshan before purchase?
faqs.a: Within limits. The call is short and cargo work continues, so the visit covers deck, hatch coamings, lashing structure, accommodation, engine room and any scrubber system, plus ballast tanks the master can release. Holds cannot be entered with cargo on board. If the buyer needs more, the brokers can ask whether the ship has a longer stay or a docking coming.

faqs.q: Can the report be shared with a Chinese leasing company or bank?
faqs.a: Yes, with the client's agreement. The report can be addressed to the buyer and the lessor or bank together, and laid out as a dated condition record that a credit committee can follow without having boarded. If the lessor has its own template, send it in advance. The scope stays the same whoever the report is addressed to.

faqs.q: Do you inspect ships classed with China Classification Society?
faqs.a: Yes. The inspection works the same way whatever the class. CCS records reach the buyer through the society with the seller's consent, and the team compares its on-board readings with the last CCS thickness report where it is released. Class status, conditions of class and survey due dates come from those records, not from the inspection.

faqs.q: Can the inspection be done at a lower Yangtze or Zhoushan yard instead?
faqs.a: Yes, if the seller is docking the ship before delivery, and it often gives the buyer the fullest view: dry bottom, open tanks and staging in place. The yard runs its own contractor registration and safety induction, arranged through the seller or the yard. Repairs in progress are recorded apart from the original condition, so the buyer can tell the two apart.
